instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires any person who receives or is entitled to receive more than the threshold compensation/reimbursement in a calendar quarter to communicate directly to influence legislation/administrative action to register, including as part of regular employment.
Registrations expire each December 31 unless the registrant submits a renewal form and fee, creating an annual (12-month) renewal cycle.

During regular session, amended registration reflecting changes in client/subject matter must be filed not later than the fifth day after the first direct communication on the new client/subject matter; otherwise §305.005(k) ties amendment timing to other deadlines rather than a fixed day-count.
A person required to register must file the registration form and fee not later than the fifth day after the first direct communication that triggers registration.

The chapter requires the lobbyist (the person who lobbies for compensation/expenditures) to register and disclose the compensating/reimbursing persons as clients on the lobbyist’s registration, rather than requiring the client to file a separate registration as a registrant.
The required contents of the written, verified registration are enumerated and do not include any requirement to submit a photograph.

Officers/employees of state government branches and of political subdivisions are not required to register under the compensation-based trigger (with specified exceptions), reflecting an exemption for public officials acting in their governmental roles.

The statute provides special, reduced obligations for government actors (e.g., exemption from certain registration requirements and a separate, rule-based listing regime for political subdivision officers/employees), indicating partial relief from the rules applied to non-government lobbyists.
